subject: Cross-border data paths & subprocessor inventory — Meridian Bank Q&A
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@meridianbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on processing locations and subprocessors

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this call with Meridian last week. Our security and procurement teams are putting together the vendor packet and have three high-priority questions we need answered before we can move to legal review:

1) Where is customer request data processed and stored (regions by default and any cross-border flows)?
2) Which subprocessors are in the processing path (compute, logging, telemetry, backups) and their locations?
3) What are Redwood's default retention windows for inference logs, cached KV, and audit logs, and how do we request deletions?

We need an overview we can share with our Legal/InfoSec. Appreciate a short bulletized response and any inventory you can attach.

Regards,
Samira Khan
Sr. Product Security Manager
Meridian Bank

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@meridianbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations and subprocessors

Hi Samira — thanks, this is great to get early. High-level answers first, then I can attach our subprocessor inventory and a simple dataflow diagram:

1) Processing & storage (hosted mode):
- Default compute regions: US (primary: us-west-2) and EU (primary: europe-west1) for customers who opt into EU residency.
- Short-running inference requests are handled in the region selected by the customer. In some cases (failover or autoscale), requests may be proxied through our control plane in a different region — we document this and can disable cross-region fallbacks for Dedicated/Private deployments.

2) Subprocessors (summary):
- Compute: AWS (us-west-2), GCP (europe-west1) — used depending on model placement and capacity.
- Logging & backups: CloudVault (US/EU endpoints).
- Telemetry & metrics: TelemetryInc (US).
- Autoscaling partner (burst capacity in APAC/EU): NimbusTech (partner) — engaged only when customers opt into burst/edge options.

3) Retention & deletion:
- Inference request logs (short metadata, no training): default 30 days.
- KV/prefix cache: typically ephemeral, default TTL 24–72 hours unless customer pins longer.
- Audit logs: 365 days (retained for operations/SLA and compliance).
- We do not use customer request content to train models by default; explicit opt-in is required.
- Deletion: customers can file a deletion request via Console or Support (see attached process doc). Deletions are processed within 72 hours for hosted accounts; for Dedicated/Private we provide procedures to wipe local storage or provide scripts for on-prem.

I'll attach the subprocessor inventory and a small dataflow diagram. If Legal needs a formal subprocessor attestation we can route that to our Security team.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hannah — quick internal note before we send the packet to Meridian Legal: two points to confirm for them explicitly so they don't flag the default failover behavior:

- Can you confirm whether control-plane metadata (routing decisions, traces) ever includes plaintext customer prompts? We encrypt at rest, but Legal will want to know what is present in traces.
- For customers that require strict EU-only processing, do we have a documented configuration toggle to pin compute + logging to europe-west1 and disable cross-region fallback? If so, include the exact wording and any operational caveats.

Evelyn — FYI, they may request a subprocessor-specific DPA clause around NimbusTech since it's an ops partner used for burst capacity.

Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@meridianbank.com>, CloudOps Partner - NimbusTech <cloudops@nimbustech.io>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on processing locations and subprocessors

Thanks — answers below and I've attached the inventory + procedure docs.

- Control-plane traces: We do log routing metadata (timestamps, region ID, model variant) but we do not persist full plaintext prompts in control-plane traces for hosted customers. Where prompt content is temporarily present for debugging, it is redacted and retained only per the request-log retention window (default 30 days). All logs are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). See attached encryption-and-keys-summary.txt.

- EU-only pinning: Yes. For customers that require EU residency we offer a Residency toggle in the Console that pins compute + logging to europe-west1 and disables automatic cross-region failover. For Dedicated/Private we provide a region-lock configuration and a checklist for infra (we'll provide a Region Lock SOP when Legal asks). Caveat: pinning may reduce burst capacity during load spikes; we recommend a defined SLA and dedicated capacity for sustained throughput.

Attachments included: subprocessor inventory (redwood-subprocessors-202603.pdf), dataflow diagram (dataflow-diagram- meridian-2026-03.png), and a short encryption/keys summary (encryption-and-keys-summary.txt).

If Meridian Legal wants a formal DPA addendum listing NimbusTech and CloudVault, loop in our Security team (security@redwood.ai) and we'll start the attestation process.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah — this is perfect, thank you. A couple quick asks before we close: 

- Can you provide the Region Lock SOP and the short DPA clause that references NimbusTech and CloudVault? Our Legal wants the clause text to slot into the master DPA.
- Procurement would like a 30-minute follow-up next week to confirm timelines and deletion SLA language. Can you propose 2 slots?

If you can drop the SOP and the DPA snippet as separate attachments, I can circulate internally and get back with questions. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Samira
